top.line: An early access programme for Agent Behaviour Policies, with customers.
top.para: The workflow and mapping are in place; what is left is execution. A first group of friendlies becomes our first customers: each starts with credit on a site that meters and bills, follows a start-here page, and is followed closely. The aim is the usage moment: the simplest useful policy, the easiest entry and a fair price.

in-short.line: Seven points: ready, execution, customers, follow-up, a site, discovery, the next batch.
in-short.para: Agent Behaviour Policies are ready for the next level and what is left is execution. Call the first group customers, each with credit. Follow each closely, with objectives and milestones. Give them a dedicated site with a start-here page. Discover the simplest useful policy, the easiest entry and the price. Keep a mailing list for the next batch.

now.line: Why now: the pieces are in place, and the people are ready.
now.para: A workflow that works, a mapping to what regulators ask for, and an understanding of how it fits together. What is left is execution, with a first group of engaged friendlies: consultants who will sell it and already use some of it, people I work with, and us.

customers.line: Why they are customers, not beta users.
customers.para: Beta describes the product; customers describe the relationship. Each starts with credit, £5, £50 or another number, on a site we run, so use is metered from day one and the question of what they would pay is real. It is the newsroom's own idea: give it for free until the value is there.

site.line: A dedicated site, with a start-here page and a page per customer.
site.para: A dedicated site would help a lot: one place to follow how everyone is getting on, with a start-here page of clear instructions, and a page for each customer with their objectives and milestones. The billing exists already: this newsroom meters every page against credit, and its top-up link has been live since 11 October.

follow.line: Hand-holding on purpose, daily if needed.
follow.para: We would like to really invest in following up: an email every day if it helps, specific hand-holding, and objectives for each customer. It will not scale and is not meant to yet. Paul Graham: recruit users manually, set them up on the spot, and make up for an early product with attentiveness.

discover.line: What we want to discover: the usage moment.
discover.para: The moment a policy becomes worth something to one person. Three questions: the simplest useful policy, perhaps a system prompt as a policy or one agent's reach; the entry point with least friction, since the pages have been hard to understand; and the price. Track start, first policy, rows and gaps, milestones, credit used and top-ups.

batches.line: Batches, not a launch, and a mailing list for the next.
batches.para: The first batch is small enough to follow closely. Everyone else who asks goes on a mailing list, with what they want to use it for. The next batch gets a start-here page made from what the first taught us, and less hand-holding per customer.

limits.line: What this brief does not claim.
limits.para: The programme, its site, the start-here page and the mailing list are proposed. Prices are not set; £5 and £50 are starting points to test. The metering is real but is this newsroom's today. No customer is named. The policies, the vocabulary and this brief are open under CC BY 4.0.

sources.para: A voice memo of 20 October 2026; Paul Graham's essay of July 2013; the Agent Behaviour Policy at abp.sgit.ai; and related articles on paying after the value, selling early, the Pellbridge agents, what an agent can reach, and system prompts as policies.
